data.why: The page is a live lookup tool; a scientist types a gene symbol, UniProt accession, or PDB code (example chips for TP53/BRCA1/EGFR/APP/ACTB/Q6L8H1 are built into the page) and all data is fetched client-side from public APIs, so no local example data needs to be staged.

goals: Resolve a gene symbol, UniProt accession, or PDB code to the canonical UniProt entry and review its function, organism, and curation status before deciding whether it is the right protein to study
Inspect high-quality 3D structures (X-ray, cryo-EM, NMR) ranked by resolution and rotate/render them in different representations to assess fold and ligand-binding surfaces
Explore the STRING protein-protein interaction network to identify binding partners and hub connectivity relevant to a pathway of interest
Survey InterPro domain, family, and site annotations to understand the protein's modular architecture
Check Reactome pathway membership and CATH/SCOP structural classification to place the protein in its broader biological and structural context
Review subcellular localization, disease associations, and the full sequence (with FASTA export) to prepare for downstream experimental or computational analysis

review.summary: The tree describes ProteinScope's purpose and main panels well, its depth and wording are mostly sound, and every screen I opened matches its node. Before filing it needs fixes: the search behaviour is described wrongly (gene symbols nearly always go to a picker that can leave out the canonical protein), two scientific caveats are missing (classification cards for partner chains, peptide complexes ranked first), and the citation and classification features are missing.
